title: Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations
takeaway: Candidate generation and final ranking serve different objectives and can be maintained as separate stages.
decision: Preserve topic and language constraints during retrieval, then personalize only eligible candidates. Do not claim the local weighted ranker is a trained deep model.

title: Adapting the Facebook Reels RecSys AI Model Based on User Feedback
takeaway: Direct interest feedback provides information beyond likes or watch time; sparse feedback and sampling bias still require care.
decision: Give explicit saved topics, saves and hides clear influence; provide an editable preference view rather than treating time spent as proof of satisfaction.

title: Engineering the next generation of LinkedIn’s Feed
takeaway: Content understanding, evolving interaction history, freshness and production latency jointly shape a useful feed.
decision: Keep recent topic signals distinct from longer-lived interests, use bounded history, and retain a simple explainable baseline at this project’s scale.

title: Pinterest Labs — Research & Innovation
takeaway: Pinterest describes content representations that connect pins, boards, products and queries across retrieval and ranking, with responsible AI throughout the lifecycle.
decision: Use shared content metadata across communities, bookmarks and search instead of isolated feature-specific profiles. The original pinterestlabs.com URL redirected to this actual domain.

title: Netflix Recommendations: Beyond the 5 stars (Part 1)
takeaway: This historical engineering account distinguishes rating accuracy from the whole recommendation experience and emphasizes diversity, freshness and explanations.
decision: Show why an item was recommended, diversify the list, and avoid presenting a proxy metric as demonstrated user benefit. These are historical design lessons, not current Netflix weights.

title: How to Use Our Taste Profile Feature to Shape Your Spotify Homepage
takeaway: Spotify exposes a readable interpretation of taste and permits users to steer or remove preference input.
decision: Expose interest sources and a reset/pause or chronological control so a one-off interaction does not permanently define the feed.

title: The history of Amazon’s recommendation algorithm
takeaway: Item relationships can be a practical recommendation signal; chronological evaluation better reflects predicting subsequent preferences than reconstructing old consumption.
decision: Bootstrap from metadata of genuinely saved items and selected communities, and evaluate ordering on time-separated fixtures before considering a learned model.

title: Overview of search result ranking in SharePoint Server
takeaway: Ranking combines query-dependent and query-independent features, with cheaper early stages and more selective later work.
decision: Keep query relevance separate from freshness and account affinity, and calculate expensive enrichment only for the candidates actually returned.

title: SEMORec: A Scalarized Efficient Multi-Objective Recommendation Framework
takeaway: Multiple recommendation objectives require an explicit tradeoff, and the ability to tune objective importance can matter operationally.
decision: Keep relevance, recency and diversity weights named and bounded; retain deterministic tests and user controls instead of an opaque single engagement score.

title: How TikTok recommends videos #ForYou
takeaway: The published explanation separates strong and weak feedback, cold-start interests, negative controls and deliberate interruption of repetitive patterns.
decision: Offer not-interested feedback, deduplicate results, and avoid repeated same-source runs while keeping explicit topic search relevant.

title: For You Home Timeline Recommendations
takeaway: X describes sourcing recent relevant candidates, interaction-based ranking, filtering and a reverse-chronological Following alternative.
decision: Separate personalized For you from a chronological Latest mode and ensure users can hide irrelevant recommendations.

title: X’s Recommendation Algorithm — repository architecture
takeaway: The published repository documents distinct user-signal, candidate-source, ranking and post-mixing/filtering components.
decision: Keep event capture, interest-profile assembly and pure list ranking in separate local modules; use architectural lessons without copying repository implementation code.

title: Wide & Deep Learning for Recommender Systems
takeaway: The paper’s complete abstract explains the tradeoff between memorizing known feature interactions and generalizing to unseen combinations, including sparse-data risks.
decision: Use content metadata for cold start and bounded account evidence for affinity. Defer learned embeddings until sufficient legitimate training data exists.

title: ACM RecSys 2026 — Call for Contributions
takeaway: The conference’s evaluation guidance values reproducibility, user control, diversity and metrics beyond accuracy, with evidence aligned to claims.
decision: Document ranking inputs and limitations, add reproducible tests for intended behavior, and avoid claiming increased retention from source review or unit tests.

title: SciPy cosine distance reference
takeaway: Cosine distance is one minus normalized dot-product similarity; confusing distance with similarity reverses ranking intent.
decision: Use normalized, bounded affinity and explicit zero-evidence behavior in ranking tests. This successfully read source replaces the IEEE bot-verification shell.

title: Stanford CS246 — Recommender Systems I
takeaway: The course distinguishes content-based and collaborative methods and identifies cold start, sparsity, first-rater and popularity-bias limitations.
decision: Start with content-based topic overlap plus explicit user choices; reserve some source variety instead of assuming popularity is universal relevance.

title: Optimizing Search Engines using Clickthrough Data
takeaway: Clicks depend on the displayed ranking as well as relevance; an unclicked item may simply have been unseen, so a click is not an absolute relevance judgment.
decision: Do not interpret all unclicked stories as dislikes. Weight explicit hides and saves distinctly, and use impression-aware evaluation before learning from click logs.

title: Technique protects privacy when making online recommendations
takeaway: MIT describes privacy risks in feature-vector recommendation and research separating useful nearest-neighbor output from unnecessary disclosure.
decision: Keep each interest profile private to its account, bound retained event metadata, and do not expose other users’ histories. The project does not claim to implement the paper’s cryptographic protocol.

title: RecSys Challenge 2024 — News recommendation task and evaluation
takeaway: News recommendation combines rapidly decaying items and implicit interests; evaluation includes nDCG/MRR/AUC and diversity, novelty, serendipity and coverage.
decision: Apply recency decay to news, deduplicate repeated stories and test source coverage alongside relevance; do not optimize only clicks.

title: A Survey of Accuracy Evaluation Metrics of Recommendation Tasks
takeaway: The complete published abstract explains that evaluation metrics must match the task; an inappropriate metric can select the wrong algorithm.
decision: Use ordering and coverage checks appropriate to a news feed, and label offline results separately from real user outcomes. This source replaces unreadable RecBole pages.

title: TensorFlow Recommenders — Recommending movies: retrieval
takeaway: The tutorial separates efficient candidate retrieval from fine ranking and illustrates training/test preparation and implicit versus explicit evidence.
decision: Keep the current retrieval/ranking boundary explicit and measure a simple baseline before adding training infrastructure; absence of interaction is not a product-level dislike signal.

title: Introduction to TorchRec
takeaway: Embedding representations are trained from labeled examples; large-scale recommendation tables require deliberate memory and infrastructure planning.
decision: Do not label random or untrained vectors as intelligence. Use real account metadata and transparent rules now, and keep a future learned-model interface separate.

title: scikit-learn — ndcg_score
takeaway: nDCG discounts lower-ranked items and normalizes against the ideal ordering; cutoff and tie handling affect the measured result.
decision: When graded relevance labels exist, evaluate top-k ordering with a documented cutoff and tie policy; retain deterministic order for equal scores.
